why_a_rule_at_all: The plan gates stage C on two conditions -- deadline reserve AND prior discrimination -- and neither is a table the earlier commands produce. Left implicit, 'stage B finished' reads as 'stage C starts', and the phase spends ~20 GPU-hours on a decision nobody made. `stage-c` answers go/no-go over three conditions, ALL required, and writes runs/architecture/<tag>-stage-c.{json,md}.
the_three_conditions: discrimination -- the measured BPB spread across the stage's arms against the spread their own parameter mismatch could explain at PARAM_SCALING_EXPONENT (0.34). A grid matched to a few percent can move BPB on size alone; a measured spread inside that width is a ranking of the matching residual, and 1B tokens buys a more precise version of the same confound. finalists -- at most two arms (the plan's cap) carrying no MEASURED failure, in Pareto order; `unproven` stays eligible because a column with no power at proxy scale is exactly what more tokens might resolve, `blocked` does not. deadline -- 1B tokens per finalist plus the control, costed per arm from the tokens/hour the previous stage's metrics.jsonl actually recorded, against the controller's own remaining window.
the_honesty_note: Every other rule in architecture_report.py was committed before the numbers it judges. This one could not be -- 'did the previous stage separate its arms' is a question about a finished table, and stage B's table was already on screen. The guard is that it introduces NO new threshold: the exponent is stage A's, the 1B budget and the two-finalist cap are the plan's, the window is the controller's. It also records `go_would_have_required` so the boundary can be read against the observation instead of taken on trust. If you are tempted to adjust anything in it after reading the verdict, that is the thing it was built to make visible.
known_limitation_of_the_discrimination_t: It is one-sided. A measured spread inside the parameter confound is also what a genuine architectural effect cancelling against the residual would look like, and the two are indistinguishable at this scale. That is stated in the module rather than argued away, and it is itself a reason not to spend a stage ranking the shapes -- not a reason to call the stage decisive.
